explanation: A prophet in the Old Testament who performed miracles and spoke God's word to the people of Israel.
A mountain, also known as Mount Sinai, where Moses received the Ten Commandments from God.
A dry and inhospitable landscape with little vegetation and rainfall, where Elijah fled after killing the prophets of Baal.
Black birds that God sent to feed Elijah while he was in the wilderness.
Spiritual beings created by God who serve and carry out His will.
A biblical time period symbolizing a long and significant duration.
A natural hollow in the rock where Elijah sought shelter and met with God.
A quiet and gentle sound through which God spoke to Elijah at Horeb.
People from Syria, a land north of Israel, mentioned as enemies of Israel.
A Syrian king whom God instructed Elijah to anoint.
An Israelite general who became king over Israel after God instructed Elijah to anoint him.
A prophet and disciple of Elijah, chosen by God to succeed Elijah as prophet.
